pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all 3 seeded items are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js `item` prefixes '★ ' only when starred. The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list with one starred item.
The starred view filters WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id. The 'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and expects id order.
`show` defaults to 'all'. The 'AC-4' test checks both / and /?show=all against the exact list.
The nav link is per view. The 'AC-5' test checks the exact anchors on both views.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) returns false for anything else, which gives a 400 before any query runs. The 'AC-6' test covers 'Starred', 'none', empty and '__proto__', and checks there is no <li>.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. The 'AC-7' test asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs was updated so the route passes validation.

findings.what: The README mentions ?show=starred but not the ★ marker, the 'Starred only' / 'All items' links, or the 400 for other show values.
findings.fix: Add one line covering the marker, the links and the 400.

findings.what: The AC-7 test only checks the JSON file contents. test/traffic.test.js does not exercise a query-string route end to end, although the fake app was changed to record the query.
findings.fix: Optionally add a traffic test that runs a round with '/?show=starred' and checks that the worker requests it with its query intact.

lenses.note: A spec with the owner's go exists. The behaviour matches it, and nothing beyond it was added except the traffic-check relaxation, which the PR discloses and the new route needs.
All 7 acceptance items are met and all 4 state rows have tests. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, and no acceptance item was edited after the go.
The tests assert exact outputs. I could not run them because `npm test` failed with 'vitest: not found' (dependencies not installed). The review rests on reading them.
The README was updated, but only partly (see the low finding).
The `show` handling is correct, using Object.hasOwn to avoid prototype keys. The SQL is static, built from a fixed view table.
Titles are still escaped by escapeHtml. The `show` input is allow-listed and never reaches the SQL. No secrets or planted instructions found.
The page is a minimal HTML list with a link. The diff has no CSS or UI framework files.
No UI flow is specified beyond plain links, and the tests cover the pages. No browser session is available.
The PR claims are consistent with the diff: the tests, the traffic check change and the migration all match. The title is 'Star items and show only the starred ones', under 72 characters.
